findings.title: KAROS_EMPLOYEE's client-context picker is structurally always empty — the layout never passes them a client list
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_EMPLOYEE at any width ≥md, from any workspace page, click the "Client context" row at the foot of the rail → the dropdown opens and shows "No clients found", even when the employee has assigned clients. The only way into client view is /clients → click a row.
findings.detail: The campaign widened the picker's gate from admin-only to `isStaff` (sidebar.tsx:617; baseline ddcef3e gated it at `user.role === "KAROS_ADMIN"`, sidebar.tsx:435 there) and justified it in-code: "`clients` is already fenced to their assigned clients by the app layout" (sidebar.tsx:614-616). That claim is false at HEAD. `clients` is declared `[]` at layout.tsx:46 and assigned ONLY inside `if (adminData)` at layout.tsx:105-108; `adminData` resolves to `null` for anyone who is not KAROS_ADMIN (layout.tsx:59-64). The employee-scoped list the layout does build — `staffClients` at layout.tsx:53-54 — is consumed only to make the name map at layout.tsx:56 and is never handed to Sidebar. So layout.tsx:225 passes `[]`, and sidebar.tsx:174-176 renders the "No clients found" empty state. The X that clears the context (sidebar.tsx:137-147) does work, so the F113 escape hatch survives; it is the switcher half that is dead. This is a control the campaign lit up for a role it cannot serve.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass the already-fetched scoped list: `clients={isStaffViewer ? staffClients : clients}` at layout.tsx:225 (or assign `clients = staffClients` for the employee branch), and delete the now-true-by-construction comment at sidebar.tsx:614-616.

findings.title: Client shell's "Settings" is built as a nav item and then never rendered in the nav — it hides in a credits pill and an account dropdown
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at ≥md, look at the left rail: Dashboard · AI Agents · Calendar · Workspace. Settings is not in that group. To reach /clients/[id]/settings you must either click the "Credits" pill (which reads as a balance, not a settings link) or open the avatar dropdown at the very bottom and pick Settings.
findings.detail: This is the exact shape of the owner's worked example, in the client shell. `settingsItem` is declared as a `NavItem` — same type, same icon field, same shape as the four rail tabs (client-rail.tsx:88) — but `primaryNav.map(...)` at client-rail.tsx:128 iterates `primaryNav` only (client-rail.tsx:82-87), and the mobile tab bar is fed the same `primaryNav` at client-rail.tsx:248. `settingsItem.href` is consumed in three non-nav places instead: the credits pill at client-rail.tsx:190-199, the mobile credits pill at client-rail.tsx:234-241, and `AccountMenu`'s dropdown row at account-menu.tsx:87-93 (via the `settingsHref` prop passed at client-rail.tsx:209). Worse, the desktop credits pill is conditional on `spendableCredits != null` (client-rail.tsx:189), so for a client with no credits doc the ONLY on-screen route to their own settings page at desktop width is two clicks inside the avatar dropdown. A control that is typed as a nav row and belongs beside the other four belongs in the nav group.
findings.suggestedFix: Render `settingsItem` as the fifth row of the rail nav (client-rail.tsx:127-152) and keep the account-menu row as the secondary path; the credits pill can stay as a balance readout that happens to link there.

findings.title: A CLIENT_USER whose client document is gone gets the STAFF sidebar, and two of its nav rows 404
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER whose `clientId` points at a deleted client, load any page → you get the staff shell instead of the client rail. Click the rail's "Dashboard" row → /clients/<deleted-id> → 404. Click "AI Agents" → /clients/<deleted-id>/agents → 404.
findings.detail: layout.tsx:111-211 only returns the ClientRail shell when `user.role === "CLIENT_USER" && user.clientId` AND `getClient(user.clientId)` resolves truthy (layout.tsx:112, :113 `if (client)`). When the client doc is missing the function falls through to the staff workspace return at layout.tsx:214-249, mounting Sidebar for a CLIENT_USER. Inside Sidebar, `clientHomePath` is non-null because it only checks that `user.clientId` is set (sidebar.tsx:400-401), so the Dashboard row is rewritten to `/clients/<deleted-id>` (sidebar.tsx:411) and an "AI Agents" row is spliced in at `/clients/<deleted-id>/agents` (sidebar.tsx:414-422). Both destinations reach their `notFound()`: clients/[id]/page.tsx:31 does not redirect because `user.clientId === id`, then :37 `if (!client) notFound()`; clients/[id]/agents/page.tsx:50 likewise passes through and :56 calls `notFound()`. `shouldBlockForOnboarding` does not intercept — it only fires for `hasCompletedOnboarding === false` (src/lib/onboarding.ts:9-10, :23), so any pre-existing account reaches this. Pre-campaign code had the same fallthrough (baseline layout.tsx:73-75), so this is latent, not a regression.
findings.suggestedFix: In layout.tsx, when a CLIENT_USER's client cannot be resolved, render a dedicated "workspace unavailable" shell (or redirect to a support page) rather than falling through to the staff Sidebar; and make `clientHomePath` in sidebar.tsx a prop the layout only sets when the client actually resolved.

findings.title: CLIENT_USER has no sign-out control below md — LogoutButton is only inside the desktop-only aside
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px, from any page, tap the "Company" tab in the bottom bar → the sheet shows Settings, Team (group admins), Notifications, Support, Dark mode — and no sign-out. There is no other menu at this width: the top strip is wordmark + credits pill only.
findings.detail: `LogoutButton` has exactly two mounts in the app shells (grep: src/pending/page.tsx aside): account-menu.tsx:99 and sidebar.tsx:739. `AccountMenu` is mounted once, at client-rail.tsx:209, inside the `<aside className="relative z-30 hidden w-72 shrink-0 … md:block">` opened at client-rail.tsx:102 — so it is not painted below md. The narrow-width Company sheet tail (client-rail.tsx:280-320) enumerates Settings (:284), Team (:293), NotificationBell (:307), ContactUsButton (:317) and ThemeSwitch (:319), and stops. The staff twin of that same sheet DOES carry `<LogoutButton compact />` at sidebar.tsx:739, which is what makes the omission legible as an oversight rather than a policy. Baseline ddcef3e's client sheet also lacked it, so the gap predates the campaign — but the campaign built the staff sheet with logout and left the client one without, so the asymmetry is new.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<LogoutButton compact />` to the client Company sheet tail after ThemeSwitch (client-rail.tsx:319), mirroring sidebar.tsx:739.

findings.title: A group-admin CLIENT_USER can only reach /team by shrinking the browser — the link exists solely in the mobile sheet
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER with `isGroupAdmin` at ≥md, there is no Team row in the rail nav and no Team row in the avatar dropdown. Narrow the window below md, tap Company → a "Team" row appears. /team is otherwise reachable only by typing the URL.
findings.detail: The only `/team` href a CLIENT_USER can reach is client-rail.tsx:292-301, gated on `user.isGroupAdmin` and rendered inside `MobileCompanySheet`, which is `fixed … md:hidden` (mobile-shell.tsx:156). The desktop rail's `primaryNav` (client-rail.tsx:82-87) has no Team item, and `AccountMenu`'s action block (account-menu.tsx:85-95) renders ThemeSwitch, Settings and ContactUsButton only. team/page.tsx:12 explicitly admits this role (`if (user.role === "CLIENT_USER" && !user.isGroupAdmin) redirect("/dashboard")`), so the destination is live and role-correct — it just has no desktop entrance. Note the irony: sidebar.tsx:407 builds a Team row for exactly this role, but that Sidebar branch only ever renders for a CLIENT_USER whose client did not resolve (see the 404 finding), i.e. the one case where /team is useless.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the Team row in the client rail's desktop nav (or in AccountMenu's action block) under the same `user.isGroupAdmin` condition used at client-rail.tsx:292.

findings.title: For a clientless CLIENT_USER three different nav controls all land on Workspace, two of them mislabelled
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER with no `clientId` (staff-shell fallback), click "Dashboard" → /dashboard → redirected to /assets → redirected to /tasks. Click "Assets" → /assets → /tasks. Click "Workspace" → /tasks. Click the "Karos Labs" wordmark → /dashboard → /tasks. Four controls, one page; the Workspace row lights up every time.
findings.detail: layout.tsx:111 requires `user.clientId`, so a clientless CLIENT_USER falls through to the staff Sidebar (layout.tsx:214-229). `adminItems` (sidebar.tsx:405-413) keeps every NAV row whose `roles` include CLIENT_USER: Dashboard (sidebar.tsx:53), Meetings (:57), Assets (:58), Calendar (:59), Workspace (:60). `clientHomePath` is null here, so Dashboard keeps `/dashboard`, which redirects this role at dashboard/page.tsx:17 (`redirect(user.clientId ? … : "/assets")`), and /assets redirects the role again at assets/page.tsx:25 (`if (user.role === "CLIENT_USER") redirect("/tasks")`). The wordmark links `/dashboard` in both the rail (sidebar.tsx:584) and the mobile top bar (sidebar.tsx:747), so it collapses the same way. NAV listing `/assets` with `CLIENT_USER` in its `roles` (sidebar.tsx:58) is the root inconsistency — that route refuses the role unconditionally.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop `CLIENT_USER` from the `/assets` NAV entry's roles (sidebar.tsx:58) since assets/page.tsx:25 refuses the role outright, and give the clientless CLIENT_USER case its own minimal nav rather than the filtered staff NAV.

findings.title: Notification panel footed "View workspace →" when its only rows are agent review jobs, which the workspace board provably does not contain
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_ADMIN with drafts in review and no pending tasks, open the account menu → Notifications → the panel lists N "<agent> finished a draft" rows and is footed "View workspace →". Click it → /tasks → the cross-client task board, which contains no job rows at all.
findings.detail: The footer's own comment claims "one link per KIND of row actually in the feed" (notification-bell.tsx:332-334), but the condition at :337 is `taskAlerts.length > 0 || visibleJobs.length > 0` — review jobs are lumped under the task destination. /tasks for staff renders `<TasksBoard tasks={annotatedTasks} …>` (tasks-body.tsx:192) where `annotatedTasks` derives from `listClientTasks({ limit: 500 })` (tasks-body.tsx:173-187); TasksBoard's props are `tasks: BoardTask[]` only (tasks-board.tsx:485-492) and it reads no job data. The rows themselves know the right destination — each links `/jobs/${j.jobId}` (notification-bell.tsx:276) — so the footer contradicts its own rows. Same class as finding #143's fix, one row-kind short. Baseline had the same `/tasks` footer, so this is a survivor rather than a regression.
findings.suggestedFix: Split the condition at notification-bell.tsx:337 — `taskAlerts.length > 0` footers "View workspace →", and a separate `visibleJobs.length > 0 && !viewerIsClient` branch footers "View all jobs →" to /jobs.

findings.title: The client profile panel — and its two edit buttons — is mounted in the staff shell only below md
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_ADMIN in client context at 1280px, the rail shows the client chip, Documents, Competitor Track and Brand Colors — no team size/category chips and no "Edit brand profile" / "Edit company profile" buttons. Shrink below md, tap Company → all of it appears at the top of the sheet.
findings.detail: `ClientProfilePanel` has three mounts app-wide (grep): sidebar.tsx:665, client-rail.tsx:155 and client-rail.tsx:258. The client shell mounts it at both widths; the staff shell mounts it ONLY inside `MobileCompanySheet`, which is `md:hidden` (mobile-shell.tsx:156). The staff desktop `clientSections` block (sidebar.tsx:499-575) renders the chip (:506-542), ClientDocuments (:544-555), CompetitorTrack (:560-565) and BrandColorsSection (:567-573) and never the profile panel. So the panel's `setBrandProfileOpen` and `setEditing` triggers (client-profile-panel.tsx:239-252) are staff-reachable only at phone width. The data is editable elsewhere for staff (/clients/[id]/settings Profile tab), so this is width-asymmetry rather than total unreachability — but the two shells now disagree about what the rail contains, and the campaign introduced the sheet, so the asymmetry is new.
findings.suggestedFix: Either mount `ClientProfilePanel` in the staff desktop `clientSections` (sidebar.tsx:499-575, replacing or above the hand-rolled chip block at :506-542) or drop it from the staff sheet so the two widths agree.

findings.title: The client chip's ↗ means two different things depending on data, is a self-declared duplicate in one of them, and exists at no width below md
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_ADMIN in client context at 1280px, hover the client chip's ↗: for a client WITH a website it opens the external site in a new tab; for a client WITHOUT one the identical icon navigates in-app to /clients/[id] — which the "Dashboard" tab three rows above already points to. At 375px the ↗ is absent entirely.
findings.detail: CD-G4 repointed the ↗ at the client's real website (sidebar.tsx:484-489, :520-530) — baseline ddcef3e had it as an internal `<Link href={`/clients/${id}`}>` (baseline sidebar.tsx:373-380). But the null-website branch at sidebar.tsx:532-539 keeps the old internal link, which the campaign's own comment calls redundant with the nav's Dashboard tab (sidebar.tsx:479-483, tab defined at sidebar.tsx:72). So one glyph, one tooltip position, two behaviours (new tab vs same-tab route), one of them a known duplicate path. Separately, the whole chip block (sidebar.tsx:506-542) lives only in `clientSections`, rendered inside `shellContent` (sidebar.tsx:607) which mounts in the `hidden … md:block` aside (sidebar.tsx:792-794) and in the drawer (sidebar.tsx:784) — and the drawer is inside the `!clientCtx` branch (sidebar.tsx:744-788), so with a client context active below md neither renders. The narrow-width sheet substitutes `ClientProfilePanel` (sidebar.tsx:665), which contains no website anchor anywhere (client-profile-panel.tsx:221-300).
findings.suggestedFix: Render the ↗ only when `clientSiteHref` is non-null (drop the sidebar.tsx:532-539 fallback, since Dashboard already covers it), and surface the same website ↗ in the narrow-width sheet — either on ClientProfilePanel's company header or as its own row.

findings.title: Staff cannot switch to a different client below md — the sheet offers exit but no picker
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_EMPLOYEE or KAROS_ADMIN at 375px with client context active, tap Company → the sheet offers Settings, Notifications, Support, Dark mode, "Exit client view", Sign out. To reach a different client you must Exit → land on /clients → tap a row. There is no switcher at this width.
findings.detail: `ClientContextPicker` is rendered once, inside `shellContent` (sidebar.tsx:617-619). `shellContent` has exactly two call sites: the mobile drawer (sidebar.tsx:784) and the desktop aside (sidebar.tsx:793). The drawer sits inside the `clientCtx ? … : …` false-branch (sidebar.tsx:743-788), and the aside is `hidden … md:block` (sidebar.tsx:792). So when `clientCtx` is non-null (sidebar.tsx:433) and the viewport is below md, the only chrome painted is `MobileTabBar` (sidebar.tsx:657-662) and `MobileCompanySheet` (sidebar.tsx:664-741), neither of which contains the picker. The exit button at sidebar.tsx:728-738 makes it a detour rather than a dead end, which is why this is low.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<ClientContextPicker clients={clients} isAdmin={…} />` to the staff Company sheet tail (sidebar.tsx:699-740), above "Exit client view" — and fix the empty-list bug first, or it will be dead for employees there too.

findings.title: Two different "Workspace" destinations one sheet apart in staff client-context mode
findings.clickPath: As a KAROS_ADMIN at 375px with client context active: the bottom bar's "Workspace" tab goes to /clients/[id]/tasks (that client's Progress view). Tap Company → Notifications → the panel's footer "View workspace →" goes to /tasks (the cross-client board). Same word, two pages, both reachable in the same gesture.
findings.detail: `clientViewNav` labels `/clients/${clientId}/tasks` as "Workspace" (sidebar.tsx:75) and that list feeds both the rail nav (sidebar.tsx:426, :606) and the bottom tab bar (sidebar.tsx:657-658). The bell mounted inside the same sheet (sidebar.tsx:711-718) footers its feed with a hard-coded `/tasks` (notification-bell.tsx:338), which for staff renders the cross-client board (tasks-body.tsx:190-193) because /tasks passes no `viewClientId` (tasks/page.tsx:6-9, tasks-body.tsx:30, :49-52). Navigating there leaves all four tab-bar tabs unlit while the context bar still names the client. Cosmetically minor, but it is the same word promising two things.
findings.suggestedFix: When a client context is active, have the bell footer point at the in-context board (`/clients/${clientId}/tasks`), or rename one of the two labels.

findings.title: CLIENT_USER has no sign-out at any width below md — the campaign deleted the only phone-reachable one
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px: open any page → the desktop rail (client-rail.tsx:102, `hidden … md:block`) is not rendered, so AccountMenu and its LogoutButton never mount. Tap Company in the bottom bar → the sheet tail (client-rail.tsx:280-320) offers Settings, Team, notifications, Contact us, Theme — no sign out. Tap Settings → /clients/[id]/settings, which at baseline ddcef3e ended in an "Account" card holding a LogoutButton; at HEAD that card is gone. Tap "Account settings" → /settings, which renders SettingsForm — profile + password only, no sign out. There is no /logout route either.
findings.detail: LogoutButton is mounted in exactly two places in the workspace: account-menu.tsx:99 (reached only from client-rail.tsx:209, inside the `hidden w-72 shrink-0 … md:block` aside at client-rail.tsx:102) and sidebar.tsx:739 (staff shell only, and staff also get the inline `handleLogout` at sidebar.tsx:352 which renders in the mobile drawer via shellContent(true) at sidebar.tsx:784 — so staff are covered at every width). The third mount, /pending (src/app/pending/page.tsx:48), is outside the (app) shell. Provenance is exact: `git show ddcef3e:src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx` lines 211-219 rendered an Account card with `<LogoutButton />` on the client settings page, which is reachable at phone width through the Company sheet. HEAD removed it, and the comment left in its place — page.tsx:257-258, "which already lives in the rail's account menu" — is only true above md. Baseline's mobile sheet also had no logout, so the settings-page card was carrying the entire narrow-width case.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<LogoutButton compact />` to the client-rail mobile Company sheet tail (client-rail.tsx:280-320), next to ThemeSwitch — that is where the staff sheet already puts it (sidebar.tsx:739). Restoring the settings-page card would also work but re-creates the stranded-control shape the row was meant to remove.

findings.title: Credits pill in the client rail lands on the Channels tab, not Credits
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 1280px: rail footer shows a pill reading "Credits  340" → click → /clients/<id>/settings → SettingsTabs opens tabs[0]. For a client, profileSection is null (page.tsx:118) and is filtered out (page.tsx:231), so tabs[0] is `channels` — the page shows the connected-channels grid, and the credits balance the pill was labelled with is one further click away. Identical at 375px via the top-bar pill whose own aria-label promises "…credits remaining, open settings".
findings.detail: Both credit pills use the bare `settingsItem.href` (client-rail.tsx:88 = `/clients/<id>/settings`) with no `?tab=`: desktop Link at client-rail.tsx:190-199, mobile Link at client-rail.tsx:234-241 with aria-label `${spendableCredits} credits remaining, open settings` (client-rail.tsx:236). SettingsTabs seeds `active` from `initialTab` only when it matches a surviving tab id, else falls back to `tabs[0].id` (settings-tabs.tsx:31-33, :38). At baseline the destination was a single stacked column, so any link to the page did land on the credits section; the campaign added the tab row (page.tsx:224-231) and no inbound link was updated. Grepping the whole repo for `settings?tab=` / `tab=credits` returns zero hits — the deep-link contract documented at page.tsx:44-47 has no callers anywhere in the product.
findings.suggestedFix: Point both pills at `${settingsItem.href}?tab=credits`. The id already resolves for every role (creditsSection at page.tsx:120 is never null, so `credits` is present in the filtered list for client, employee and admin).

findings.title: "Account settings" is a detached PageHeader link sitting beside — not inside — the settings tab row
findings.clickPath: As any role: open /clients/<id>/settings → the page shows a header with a small "Account settings" text link at top-right (page.tsx:239-245) and, below the header and banner, a bordered tab row Profile · Channels · Credits · Automation · Meetings · Team (page.tsx:224-231 → settings-tabs.tsx:49-73). Clicking "Account settings" leaves the page entirely for /settings, and there is no control on /settings that returns to the row.
findings.detail: This is the owner's named defect, confirmed. The link predates the campaign (it is at ddcef3e:.../settings/page.tsx:83) but at baseline there was no tab row to belong to — the page was a stacked column, so a header link was the only available placement. The campaign introduced the row (page.tsx:224-231) without absorbing the link, producing a settings surface with two separate navigation groups. Compounding it: /settings is the personal account page (name, phone, avatar, resume, password) and it is the ONLY route to it for a CLIENT_USER — the client rail's AccountMenu row labelled "Settings" points at `settingsHref` (account-menu.tsx:88 ← client-rail.tsx:209), i.e. the company settings page, and the mobile Company sheet's Settings row does the same (client-rail.tsx:285). So changing your own password as a client is: avatar menu → Settings (company) → "Account settings" (tertiary text link in a page header) → Account Security tab. Nothing in the chrome names the personal page.
findings.suggestedFix: Make it a seventh entry in the SettingsTabs row whose content is the personal account section (or a tab that renders a link card), or — if /settings must stay a separate route — give the client rail's AccountMenu a second row "Account settings → /settings" alongside the existing company "Settings" row, and add the same row to the mobile Company sheet. Either way the control should sit with the other settings controls, not above them.

findings.title: Meetings tab links a client to transcripts that are hidden from clients — the destination 404s
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER: /clients/<id>/settings → Meetings tab → the list shows every meeting on the account, including ones staff marked hidden → click a hidden row → /transcripts/<id> calls notFound() and renders the 404 page. The client is now off the settings surface with no way back except browser Back.
findings.detail: The page fetches with `listTranscripts({ clientId: id })` (page.tsx:66) — no `excludeHiddenFromClient`. That option exists precisely for this (src/lib/data.ts:773-774, applied at :784) and the global meetings list uses it for client sessions: `listTranscripts({ clientId: user.clientId, excludeHiddenFromClient: true })` at src/app/(app)/transcripts/page.tsx:16. meetingsSection then renders `transcripts.slice(0, 12)` unfiltered (page.tsx:192) with a Link per row, while the destination refuses: `if (user.role === "CLIENT_USER") { if (t.hiddenFromClient || t.clientId !== user.clientId) notFound(); }` (transcripts/[id]/page.tsx:20-22). Pre-existing (ddcef3e settings page line 49 has the same unflagged call), but the campaign gave the list a tab of its own and so more prominence.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass `excludeHiddenFromClient: user.role === "CLIENT_USER"` in the listTranscripts call at page.tsx:66, matching transcripts/page.tsx:16.

findings.title: ?tab= silently falls back while the URL keeps the tab it did not honour

findings.detail: The degradation itself is safe and worth confirming: `tabs.some((t) => t.id === initialTab) ? initialTab : fallback` (settings-tabs.tsx:31-33) means a filtered-out id (page.tsx:231 drops tabs whose content is null) can never blank the panel or crash — `current` also re-guards at :43, and :42 returns null on an empty list. findings.suggestedFix: When `initialTab` is present but unmatched, replaceState to the canonical URL on mount (or drop the param) so the address bar matches what is shown.

findings.title: SEO/GEO panel tells the client to "ask us" to add competitors, which the client can do themselves in the rail — and offers no control either way

findings.title: Client dashboard tab row has no horizontal scroll container and clips at 375px, unlike its sibling SettingsTabs
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px, on /clients/<own-id>, scroll to the segmented control. Available width is 343px (main has px-4 at src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:177/241). "Performance" + "Search & AI visibility" at text-sm with px-4, gap-2 and a 14px icon each measure ~340-355px including the wrapper's p-1 and border, so the right edge of the "Search & AI visibility" button sits at or past the clip boundary — main is overflow-x-clip and the wrapper is a non-wrapping inline-flex with no overflow-x-auto.
findings.control: src/components/client-dashboard-tabs.tsx:57 (`mb-5 inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-2 p-1` — no overflow container, no flex-wrap)
findings.destination: src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:177 and :241 (`<main className="flex-1 overflow-x-clip px-4 …">`) — anything past the content box is clipped, not scrollable
findings.detail: Stated honestly: I can demonstrate the missing scroll container and the clipping boundary, not that the button becomes unclickable — its left portion stays in the content box, so a tap probably still registers with the label cut. What makes it worth fixing rather than ignoring as styling is the combination with finding 2: this control is the ONLY route to the client's entire visibility report, so any clipping of it is clipping of the one affordance that reaches that content. The campaign's own sibling component solved this explicitly — SettingsTabs wraps its tablist in `-mx-1 mb-6 max-w-full overflow-x-auto px-1` with the comment "this sits above a mobile view" (src/components/settings-tabs.tsx:47-52). ClientDashboardTabs and ProgressView (src/components/progress-view.tsx:98) both skipped it; ProgressView's three labels are short enough not to matter.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the control in the same `-mx-1 max-w-full overflow-x-auto px-1` container SettingsTabs uses, or shorten the second label to "Visibility" at narrow widths.

ANSWERS TO THE SPECIFIC ASKS.
(a) Attention row CTA (#97): the "N deliverables in review" row is correctly a non-link — I verified the claim behind it. getClientLibraryAssets does not strip drafts (asset-visibility.ts:16-28) and an undated draft is "unlocked" (post-chain.ts:364-371), so the row does render for a client with real drafts; isInClientArchive excludes drafts, so no client-reachable surface lists them. The two task rows below it are the defect (finding 1).
(b) Counter tiles (CD-H1/G6): all five are inert. StatCard takes no href (ui.tsx:213-232) and is rendered once — ClientAnalyticsStats at page.tsx:193 with hideStats={true} passed to ClientAnalytics at :85, so there is no duplication and no dead link. Worth flagging as data, not a finding: "Deliverables" counts client-redacted unlocked assets including drafts the client can never open anywhere, and "Agent runs" replaced a baseline card that carried an "Open AI Agents" link (ddcef3e client-analytics.tsx:125) — the counter now has no route onward, though the rail's AI Agents nav item still reaches the page.
(c) Every link out of the SEO/GEO panel: there are NO <Link>, <a>, router.push or window.location calls anywhere in seo-geo-panel.tsx, seo-geo-action-plan.tsx or seo-geo/*.tsx. Every control is in-place: Approve (server action, no navigation, seo-geo-action-plan.tsx:66-78 → approveSeoGeoRecommendationAction), ScorePopover (dialog only), Disclosure, GapList filters/expand, and 5 FlagButton sites (support dialog). The per-recommendation route is deliberately prose now — GapView.agentChip is pinned null (presenter.ts:1126-1136, gap-list.tsx:88-95) because every label it could carry named a managed product with no card at /clients/[id]/agents. Verified: no href was re-introduced. The one FlagButton that misfires by role is finding 4.
(d) Score popover: no navigation, Escape restores focus to the trigger, backdrop closes, max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] keeps it inside 375px. Clean. Note the "Do buyers find you?" subline says "Click a score…", which applies to the presence tiles only — the lifted headline ScoreTiles use InfoTip + Disclosure and are not clickable. Copy scope, not wiring.
(e) Regenerate / CD-G5: verified admin-only in UI and on the server, with an honest disabled reason (detail in finding 8). The duplicate entry point is finding 8; the missing Schedule counterpart is finding 4.
(f) Visibility-tab structure: correct — hideScores/hidePlan at page.tsx:103-104 are gated on `isClientViewer && !!seoGeo` and match the `seoGeo ?` branch at :155, so nothing renders twice and nothing behind the tab also renders outside it. Staff get the plain single stack with scores and plan inside the panel.
(g) "Must a client click a tab to see any score, and was that true at ddcef3e?" — YES at HEAD, NO at ddcef3e. Demonstrated in finding 2 against the baseline file.

NOT COVERED / OUT OF THIS CLUSTER: I traced /tasks, /clients/[id]/settings and the two shells only as far as needed to verify destinations, not as owners — the settings page's own controls (including the confirmed "Account settings" example) and the /tasks board's internal controls belong to other clusters. I did not verify the phone-width sign-out regression named in the brief (client-rail.tsx / account-menu.tsx) since it is already confirmed. findings.title: CLIENT_USER cannot sign out at phone width — the only sign-out is inside the desktop-only aside, and the campaign deleted the page-level fallback
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px on /clients/<id>: tap every tab (Dashboard, AI Agents, Calendar, Workspace) and the Company tab, open the Company sheet and scroll it to the bottom (Settings · Team · Notifications · Support · Dark mode), then go to Settings → every tab (Channels, Credits, Automation, Meetings, Team). There is no sign-out control anywhere. The user is permanently signed in until they clear cookies.
findings.detail: `LogoutButton` has exactly three mounts in the app: src/app/pending/page.tsx:48 (only reachable when user.disabled), src/components/sidebar.tsx:739 (staff shell), and src/components/account-menu.tsx:99. AccountMenu's only mount in the client shell is client-rail.tsx:209, inside `<aside className="relative z-30 hidden w-72 … md:block">` (client-rail.tsx:102) — display:none below md. The mobile Company sheet's tail group (client-rail.tsx:280-320) carries Settings, Team, Notifications, Contact us and the theme switch but no LogoutButton; the STAFF twin of the same sheet does carry it (sidebar.tsx:739, with the comment "plus … the sign-out the drawer used to carry"), so the omission is specific to the client shell. Pre-campaign there was a working phone-width path: the sheet's Settings row → the client settings page's Account card, which held `<LogoutButton />` (git show ddcef3e:src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:211-218). The campaign removed that card on an assumption that is false below md — the comment at HEAD says so in as many words: "The Account card that used to close this page held nothing but a Sign out button, which already lives in the rail's account menu" (src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:255-257). /login is a pure client page with no session check, so it offers sign-in, not sign-out. Definitive answer to the question asked: no, a CLIENT_USER cannot sign out at phone width.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<LogoutButton compact />` to the client sheet's tail group (client-rail.tsx, after ThemeSwitch) exactly as sidebar.tsx:739 does, and/or restore the Account card on the client settings page. The sheet tail is the better home — it is the client shell's phone-width equivalent of the account menu.

findings.title: Group-admin CLIENT_USER can only reach /team below md — the desktop rail has no Team link at all
findings.clickPath: As a group-admin CLIENT_USER at 1440px: the rail shows Dashboard · AI Agents · Calendar · Workspace, the account dropdown shows Theme · Settings · Support · Sign out, and Settings → Team tab shows only the join-key card. There is no route to /team (the page that actually manages team members) other than typing the URL. Narrow the window below 768px and the same link appears in the Company sheet.
findings.detail: The only `/team` link in the client shell is client-rail.tsx:292-301, rendered inside `MobileCompanySheet`, whose root is `fixed inset-0 z-50 … md:hidden` (src/components/mobile-shell.tsx:156). The destination explicitly admits a group admin (`if (user.role === "CLIENT_USER" && !user.isGroupAdmin) redirect("/dashboard")`, team/page.tsx:12) and renders a scoped roster for them (team/page.tsx:31-38). sidebar.tsx:407 contains the code that would surface this nav item for a group-admin client (`if (n.href === "/team" && user.role === "CLIENT_USER" && user.isGroupAdmin) return true;`), but the Sidebar is never rendered for a CLIENT_USER who has a clientId — src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:111-171 returns the ClientRail shell first. So that branch is dead for the role it names. Note the settings page's Team tab is not a substitute: it is `ClientKeyInline` ("Invite your team", clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:213-220), not member management. This is the exact mirror image of the sign-out defect: one control desktop-only, one control phone-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the Team row in the desktop rail too — either append it to `primaryNav` when `user.isGroupAdmin`, or add it to AccountMenu beside Settings (account-menu.tsx:87-93). One declaration, both widths.

findings.title: The "Credits" pill lands on the Channels tab, not Credits — the destination reads ?tab= and no control in the app ever sets it
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at any width, click the rail pill labelled "Credits 240" (or the mobile top-bar pill whose aria-label is "240 credits remaining, open settings") → lands on /clients/<id>/settings with no query string → SettingsTabs falls back to the first tab, which for a client is Channels (integrations/LinkedIn seats). The Credits panel the pill promised is one further click away, in a horizontally-scrolling tab strip.
findings.detail: The settings page was rebuilt to accept a deep link: `searchParams: Promise<{ tab?: string }>` with the comment "this keeps the tab component free of a Suspense requirement and seeds it from the URL on a hard load, which is what makes a ?tab= link work at all" (clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:44-51), passed to `SettingsTabs initialTab` (:259), which honours it (settings-tabs.tsx:30-32) and whose own docstring says "The active tab lives in `?tab=` so a link can point at one (support can send 'your credits are here')" (settings-tabs.tsx:22-24). A repo-wide grep for `settings?tab=` returns nothing: no control anywhere sets the param, so the mechanism has zero in-app callers. The pill is the one control whose label names a tab. It is worse than a default landing: `profileSection` is `isStaff ? <ClientEditor/> : null` (settings/page.tsx:118) and null-content tabs are filtered out (:231), so for a CLIENT_USER `tabs[0]` — the fallback at settings-tabs.tsx:29 — is `channels`, not `profile`. Both pill mounts are affected: client-rail.tsx:191 (desktop rail footer) and client-rail.tsx:235 (mobile top bar).
findings.suggestedFix: Point both pills at `${settingsItem.href}?tab=credits`. While there, use the same param for any other label-specific entry point (e.g. a "connect a channel" prompt → ?tab=channels), since the destination already supports it.

findings.title: Notification-bell rows inside the Company sheet leave the sheet open — the same same-route trap the campaign fixed for Settings and Team
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px on /tasks (the Workspace tab): tap Company → Notifications → tap a task row ("A task is waiting on you"). The bell panel closes, the route becomes /tasks?owner=client&task=<id>, but the full-screen Company sheet is still covering the page — the tap looks like it did nothing. The user must find the X at the top right before they can see the task they opened. Same for the footer's "View workspace →" on /tasks, and for any transcript row while already on /transcripts.
findings.detail: `useCompanySheet` closes the sheet in an effect keyed on `usePathname()` only (mobile-shell.tsx:60-63). `usePathname` excludes the query string, so a navigation that only changes search params never fires it. Every navigating control the bell renders is query-only or potentially same-route: TaskAlertRow's `href = /tasks?owner=…&task=…` (notification-bell.tsx:382), the footer's `/tasks` (:339) and `/transcripts` (:348), and the action-item link `/transcripts/${n.transcriptId}` (:307). Their `onClick={onClose}` closes the BELL panel (notification-bell.tsx:208/277/308/340), not the sheet — the sheet's setter is not passed down. The client rail already knows about this trap and works around it for its own two links: "Explicit close: the sheet's on-navigation effect never fires when the link's route is already current (same-route trap …)" (client-rail.tsx:281-283, applied at :286 and :295). The bell was moved into the sheet by the same campaign directive (CD-H5, client-rail.tsx:302-306) and did not get the same treatment. The Workspace tab is one of five bottom tabs, so "already on /tasks" is the common case, not an edge case.
findings.suggestedFix: Give NotificationBell an optional `onNavigate` prop and have every Link's onClick call both `onClose` and it; pass `() => setCompanyOpen(false)` from client-rail.tsx:307 and sidebar.tsx:711. Alternatively key the sheet-closing effect on `pathname + searchParams` in useCompanySheet, which fixes both shells at once.

findings.title: "Generate with AI" in the client's Brand Colors editor is enabled for a CLIENT_USER but the server action requires staff — it fails with a raw "Forbidden"
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at any width (desktop rail footer sections, or Company sheet at 375px): Brand Colors → pencil ("Edit branding guidelines") → the modal's top card "Generate from website / Karos scrapes the site or searches the web…" → click "Generate with AI" → spinner → the modal prints the literal string "Forbidden". Nothing is generated, and no wording explains that this is a staff-only action.
findings.detail: The card is gated only on `hasWebsite` (branding-modal.tsx:216), and the client shell passes `hasWebsite={!!client.website}` at both mounts (client-rail.tsx:179 desktop, client-rail.tsx:277 sheet). `website` survives the client projection (`...(c.website ? { website: c.website } : {})`, src/lib/client-visibility.ts:92), so for any client with a website on file the button renders. `generateBrandingAction` opens with `const user = await requireStaff();` (branding-actions.ts:121-122), and requireStaff throws `new Error("Forbidden")` for a CLIENT_USER (src/lib/actions/_shared.ts:11). The modal surfaces the thrown message verbatim: `setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Could not generate from website")` (branding-modal.tsx:150-151). Everything else in this modal is genuinely client-writable — `saveBrandingGuidelinesAction` uses `requireClientAccess` (branding-actions.ts:51) and even has a CLIENT_USER-specific merge path (:56-62) — so this one control is the outlier, not the panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass the viewer's staff-ness into BrandingModal (BrandColorsSection already receives `isStaff`, client-context-sections.tsx:295, and forwards `allowUsagePct={isStaff}` at :452) and gate the Generate card on it: `{hasWebsite && allowUsagePct && (…)}` — or add an explicit staff-only note instead of a button that cannot succeed.

findings.title: Meetings (/transcripts) is a client-facing page with no entry anywhere in the client shell
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at any width, there is no control that opens /transcripts unless the bell happens to hold a meeting action item: the rail/tab bar has 4 destinations (Dashboard, AI Agents, Calendar, Workspace), the Company sheet's tail has Settings/Team/Notifications/Support/Theme, and the dashboard links only to /tasks. Reaching your meeting summaries requires either the conditional bell footer, or Settings → Meetings tab → open one meeting → its "← back to /transcripts" link, or typing the URL.
findings.detail: The route serves clients deliberately: `requireUser()` with no role list, and a client-scoped branch `listTranscripts({ clientId: user.clientId, excludeHiddenFromClient: true })` plus client-specific copy "Summaries from your calls with the Karos team" (transcripts/page.tsx:11-32). The staff NAV table even declares it client-visible — `{ href: "/transcripts", label: "Meetings", icon: "Mic", roles: ["KAROS_ADMIN", "KAROS_EMPLOYEE", "CLIENT_USER"] }` (src/components/sidebar.tsx:57) — but that table drives the Sidebar, which a CLIENT_USER with a clientId never sees (layout.tsx:111-171). `primaryNav` in the client rail (client-rail.tsx:82-87) omits it. The only in-shell route is the bell footer's "View all meetings →" (notification-bell.tsx:346-354), which renders only when `visibleActions.length > 0` — i.e. only when a meeting has assigned this user an action item. Assets is handled correctly by comparison (assets/page.tsx:25 redirects a client to /tasks because the Library was merged into the Workspace archive); Meetings has no such merge and no such redirect, so the page exists and is simply unlinked.
findings.suggestedFix: Either add Meetings to `primaryNav` / the Company sheet tail, or — if four bottom tabs is the hard ceiling — put a persistent "Meetings" row in the Company sheet next to Settings and Team, and point the settings page's Meetings card header at /transcripts.

findings.title: Settings is built as a NavItem and never rendered in the desktop nav group — on desktop it lives only inside the account dropdown
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 1440px: the rail's nav group shows four rows and no Settings. Settings is reachable only by clicking the avatar chip at the bottom of the rail and picking "Settings" from the dropdown, or by clicking the "Credits" pill (which is conditional on a credits doc and, per the finding above, lands on the wrong tab). At 375px the same destination is a plain visible row in the Company sheet — so the phone treats it as navigation and the desktop hides it behind a menu.
findings.detail: `const settingsItem: NavItem = { href: `${home}/settings`, label: "Settings", icon: "Settings" };` (client-rail.tsx:88) is declared with the exact shape of the four rows the nav renders, but the nav maps `primaryNav` only (client-rail.tsx:128-151). `settingsItem` is used three times as a bare href — the credits pill (:192), `AccountMenu settingsHref` (:209 → account-menu.tsx:87-93) and the sheet row (:284) — and never as the nav row it was typed to be. This is the same shape as the confirmed "Account settings" defect on the settings page: a navigation control sitting apart from the group of navigation controls it belongs to. It is also the reason the sign-out blocker went unnoticed — everything account-shaped on desktop is behind one dropdown that stops existing below md.
findings.suggestedFix: Render `settingsItem` as a fifth row (or a footer row) in the desktop nav group, the way the Company sheet already does, and keep the dropdown copy for account-level items only.

findings.title: The Company tab's unread dot goes stale and contradicts the panel it points at
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px with exactly one meeting action item and no pending tasks: the Company tab shows a neon dot. Tap Company → Notifications → dismiss the item with its X → the panel switches to "All caught up! No pending tasks or reviews." Close the panel and the sheet: the Company tab still shows the dot, and its screen-reader text still says "1 unread notifications", until a full navigation to another route.
findings.detail: The tab dot is driven by a server prop computed once per render — `const unread = actionItems.length + reviewJobs.length + taskAlerts.length;` (client-rail.tsx:97, passed at :253, painted at mobile-shell.tsx:130-138) — while the panel's own count is recomputed from local dismissals: `visibleActions = actionItems.filter((n) => !dismissed.has(…))` and `total = visibleActions.length + visibleJobs.length + taskAlerts.length` (notification-bell.tsx:66-68, 80). The dismiss action does not revalidate the route the client is on: `dismissAssignedActionItemAction` ends with `revalidatePath("/dashboard")` only (src/lib/actions/transcript-actions.ts:329), and a CLIENT_USER is never on /dashboard (dashboard/page.tsx:17 redirects them to /clients/<id>). The comment introducing the prop claims the opposite of the observed behaviour: "The same three feeds the bell counts, so the Company tab's dot and the badge inside the sheet can never disagree (CD-H5)" (client-rail.tsx:96).
findings.suggestedFix: Either lift the dismissed set so the tab and the panel read one number, or have NotificationBell call `router.refresh()` after a successful dismiss, or add `revalidatePath("/clients/[id]", "layout")` (and /tasks, /calendar) to dismissAssignedActionItemAction so the layout prop catches up.

findings.title: Settings → Meetings lists meetings that are hidden from the client and 404s when one is tapped
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px: Company → Settings → Meetings tab → tap a row whose transcript is flagged hiddenFromClient → /transcripts/<id> renders the not-found page. The row's title and date were readable in the list before the tap.
findings.detail: The settings page fetches `listTranscripts({ clientId: id })` with no tier filter (clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:66) and renders each as a Link to `/transcripts/${t.id}` (:194) for staff and clients alike. `listTranscripts` only drops hidden rows when asked: `.filter((t) => !opts?.excludeHiddenFromClient || !t.hiddenFromClient)` (src/lib/data.ts:784) — and the client-facing /transcripts index does ask (transcripts/page.tsx:15). The detail route then refuses: `if (user.role === "CLIENT_USER") { if (t.hiddenFromClient || t.clientId !== user.clientId) notFound(); }` (transcripts/[id]/page.tsx:20-22). So the one client-reachable list of meetings that is NOT filtered links straight into a 404, and leaks the titles of meetings staff marked internal.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass `excludeHiddenFromClient: user.role === "CLIENT_USER"` to the settings page's listTranscripts call, matching transcripts/page.tsx:15.

findings.title: No account identity at phone width — the signed-in user's name and email exist only in the desktop dropdown
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER at 375px: the top bar shows the Karos wordmark and a credits pill; the Company sheet is headed "Company" and shows the client company's name, favicon, documents and competitors. Nowhere does the phone-width shell say which user account is signed in — relevant precisely because that user also cannot sign out.
findings.detail: The identity block (avatar + `user.name` + `user.email`) lives in AccountMenu's dropdown header (account-menu.tsx:63-69 trigger, :76-82 expanded), whose only client-shell mount is inside the `hidden … md:block` aside (client-rail.tsx:102, :209). findings.title: Client roster badge and agent-page badge disagree for any agent bound with "Add as live"
findings.clickPath: Staff bind an already-producing agent with BindAgentControl → "Add as live" (umbrella: launchState="live", templates=[], slotMode="single"). As a CLIENT_USER, open AI Agents: the agent's roster card carries a neutral "Not set up yet" (or "Runs on request") badge. Click the card → the detail page header and status strip carry a green pulsing "Live". The staff roster for the same client shows "Live" too, so the client's roster is the only surface that disagrees.
findings.detail: The client branch resolves each roster card's umbrella through `ownedByUmbrella = umbrellas.filter(umbrellaOwnsClientCard)` (page.tsx:124-125) and then builds `umbrellaByAgentId` from that filtered set (page.tsx:174), so `rosterStatus({launchState: umbrella?.launchState ?? null, …})` (page.tsx:189-199) receives **null** for any umbrella the filter drops. `umbrellaOwnsClientCard` (src/lib/client-agent-runs.ts:272-278) returns false for exactly one shape: `launchState === "live"` && not options-mode && no non-retired template. That is precisely what `bindClientAgentAction`'s `bindAsLive` path writes — `launchState: "live"`, `templates: []`, and `slotMode: "single"` for every agent that is not the X agent (src/lib/actions/client-agent-actions.ts:193-201). With launchState null and no active schedule, rosterStatus falls through to the `launchState === null` branch and returns "Not set up yet" / "Runs on request" (src/lib/client-agents.ts:490-499). The detail page takes the umbrella unfiltered (`umbrellas.find(u => u.customAgentId === agent.id)`, [agentId]/page.tsx:227), so its `rosterStatus` call (:255-260) sees "live" and returns Live — painted twice, in the header badge (:530) and the status strip (:561). The staff roster builds its map from the unfiltered `umbrellas` as well (page.tsx:288), so staff and client read the same agent two different ways. The same holds for a clip-maker umbrella, which by design binds with no templates (see the comment at src/components/client-agents/agent-detail-panel.tsx:220-223).
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the roster's status from the unfiltered `umbrellas` list and keep `ownedByUmbrella` for card-ownership only: build `umbrellaByAgentId` from `umbrellas` (page.tsx:174) rather than from `ownedByUmbrella`. Card selection and status resolution are two different questions and must not share one filtered set.

findings.title: Reddit agent renders posting vocabulary throughout the legacy panel
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER, AI Agents → click the Reddit agent (no umbrella bound, but it has delivered a run or has an active weekly schedule) → the page leads with the daily-finder hero ("Found today", "One thread a day, with a reply drafted in your voice") and then, directly under it, renders "Create a new post", "Create new post · N credits", a section headed "How often it posts" reading "This agent is already posting for you on a schedule", and "N credits per post".
findings.detail: `LegacyAgentPanel` hardcodes post vocabulary at lines 114-115 ("Making your next post now … finished posts appear in your Workspace"), 135 ("Create a new post"), 138-139, 148 ("Create new post · N credits"), 171 ("How often it posts"), 175 ("This agent is already posting for you on a schedule") and 186 ("N credits per post"). It accepts no `archetype` prop, and the detail page mounts it without one ([agentId]/page.tsx:640-666) even though it computed `archetype` at :288 and passes it to `AgentDetailPanel` at :612. The Reddit agent resolves to `daily_finder` (src/lib/agent-archetype.ts:96) and `AgentDetailPanel` exists specifically to avoid this — its own comment says "'Create a new post' is wrong on a clip maker and wrong on a Reddit agent" and it maps the archetype to the noun "reply" (src/components/client-agents/agent-detail-panel.tsx:19-29). The legacy branch is reached whenever there is no umbrella and (`status.tone === "live"` || `hasDelivered`) ([agentId]/page.tsx:621), which is the normal state for the intake-driven agents that run on a weekly schedule with no umbrella. "This agent is already posting for you" contradicts the hard product rule that no post-to-Reddit code path exists and a human always posts from their own account.
findings.suggestedFix: Thread `archetype` into `LegacyAgentPanel` and drive every noun from the same `OUTPUT_NOUN` map `AgentDetailPanel` uses (post / clip / reply), including the section heading ("How often it looks" for a finder) and the schedule sentence. Do not fork a second vocabulary table.

findings.title: Inputs band badges an agent "Ready to run" on a page that offers a client no way to run it
findings.clickPath: Admin grants an intake-driven agent (X / LinkedIn / Reddit) via Settings → Automation → AI agent access, no umbrella bound, no schedule, nothing delivered yet. As a CLIENT_USER, AI Agents → the card says "Not set up yet" → open it → the status strip says NOT SET UP YET, and ~200px below, the "What it runs on" band carries a green "Ready to run" badge with "This agent writes from what you saved here". There is no run control anywhere on the page.
findings.detail: With no umbrella `row` is null, `hasDelivered` is false and `status.tone` is "idle", so the hero chain falls to the `inputs ? null` arm ([agentId]/page.tsx:667-679) — deliberately silent so the inputs band owns the setup ask. But the band's badge is `view.ready ? "Ready to run" : "Needs your answers"` (src/components/client-agents/agent-sections.tsx:151-153), and `view.ready` is just `setup.ready` = whether the intake document exists (src/lib/agent-detail-sections.ts:238; src/lib/client-agent-rows.ts:206, 218, 233). Once the client has filled in their intake the band claims the agent is ready to run while `AgentDetailPanel` (umbrella-only), `ClientAgentLaunchCard` (umbrella-only) and `LegacyAgentPanel` (live-or-delivered only) are all unmounted, and `StaffAgentControls` is `isStaff`-gated (:710). The page therefore asserts readiness, contradicts its own status strip, and offers nothing to press — the client's first visit to every newly granted agent.
findings.suggestedFix: Either word the badge to what it actually knows ("Answers saved" / "Answers needed") so it stops promising a run, or have the page render a run affordance in this state. Given the CD-G1 rule that a client's run gesture lives on the detail page, the honest minimum is the copy change plus a line saying who starts the first run.

findings.title: An agent's own run history and "Last run" are computed from the client's 8 most recent jobs across ALL agents
findings.clickPath: As staff on a client with several busy agents, AI Agents → open an agent whose last run is not in the client's 8 most recent jobs → "Staff controls" reads "No runs yet." and the "This agent's runs" section is absent, while the status strip on the same screen reads e.g. "Runs on request · Last delivered 3d ago · Deliverables 12".
findings.detail: `toRunRows` sorts by createdAt and applies `.slice(0, 8)` BEFORE returning (src/lib/client-agent-rows.ts:99-102); the detail page then filters that already-truncated list down to one agent: `toRunRows(jobs, true, umbrellas).filter(run => run.agentName === agent.name)` ([agentId]/page.tsx:346-348). `listJobs({clientId})` returns every job for the client (src/lib/data.ts:385-395), so the truncation is not a data limit — it is a per-page cap being applied on the wrong side of the filter. Three things ride the result: "This agent's runs" (:782-784) silently disappears; `lastStaffRun` (:359) goes undefined so `StaffAgentControls` prints "No runs yet." (src/components/custom-agents.tsx:773-777); and `reviewHref` (:718) falls back to `/clients/${id}/assets` even though `reviewCount` (:349-358, computed from the full job list) is non-zero — so the "N ready" chip and the "N drafts waiting for review" link (custom-agents.tsx:770, 801-808) point at the client's whole asset list rather than the run holding those drafts. When the first review job IS inside the slice, the chip's count still spans every review job for the agent while the href opens only one of them.
findings.suggestedFix: Filter before capping: pass the agent-filtered jobs into `toRunRows`, or give it an explicit limit parameter and apply `.slice` after the agent filter. Derive `reviewHref` from the same unsliced review set the count comes from.

findings.title: "Run the agent →" on all three intake pages lands on a roster that has no run control
findings.clickPath: As a CLIENT_USER, AI Agents → open the Reddit agent → "Your Reddit details" → the intake page's header action "Run the agent →" → lands on /clients/[id]/agents, a grid of roster cards with no Run button anywhere; the run gesture is one more click in, inside the agent's detail page.
findings.detail: All three intake pages carry the same header link to the roster labelled "Run the agent →" (reddit-agent/page.tsx:37-42, x-agent/page.tsx:34-40, linkedin-agent/page.tsx:38-44). The label predates the campaign; the destination no longer honours it. The client branch of the roster renders only `ClientAgentRoster` (clients/[id]/agents/page.tsx:225-233), whose cards are documented as carrying "NO RUN BUTTON, deliberately and by rule" (src/components/client-agents/roster-card.tsx:20-24). The intake pages do not know the `customAgentId`, so relabelling is the low-risk fix; if the deep link is wanted, resolve the agent id for the platform on the server and link `/clients/[id]/agents/[agentId]`.

findings.title: "Manage integrations" and "Manage connections" open the default settings tab, not Channels
findings.clickPath: As staff, client AI Agents page → header action "Manage integrations →" → lands on /clients/[id]/settings, which opens the Profile tab (the client editor). Channels is a tab away. Same for "Manage connections" under "Connected accounts" on any agent detail page.

For staff, `tabs[0]` is `profile` because `profileSection` is non-null (settings/page.tsx:119, 224-231) — so the integrations link opens the client-profile editor. For a CLIENT_USER `profileSection` is null and Channels happens to become `tabs[0]`, which is why the bug is invisible in client view. The deep-link convention is already used elsewhere (`/tasks?tab=archive`).
findings.suggestedFix: Append `?tab=channels` to both hrefs. The param is already read and validated, so no destination change is needed.

findings.title: The /agents "Run an agent" client picker navigates away from the only place a staff run can be started
findings.clickPath: As staff, sidebar → Agents → the "Run an agent" card says "Agents always run against a client's context. Pick a client to launch one." Click a client chip (it carries a Play icon) → lands on /clients/[id]/agents, a roster with no run control; a run needs two more clicks (open an agent → Staff controls → Run now). Meanwhile the actual run gesture, with its own client picker, is the "Run" button on each agent card further down the page you just left.
findings.detail: The picker card (agents/page.tsx:30-55) links each active client to `/clients/${c.id}/agents` under a "Run an agent" heading. That destination's staff branch offers the bind control, the roster and cross-agent history (clients/[id]/agents/page.tsx:418-432) and no run control — CD-I1 moved every staff run gesture to `StaffAgentControls` on the per-agent route. On the very same /agents page, `CustomAgentsHub` gives each agent a `Run` button (src/components/custom-agents.tsx:565-586) that opens `RunCustomAgentModal` with the eligible-client picker inside it (:595-607). So the page has two routes to "run an agent": one that works in place, and one that navigates to a page which cannot. This is the owner's worked-example shape — a control sitting apart from the group of controls it belongs to.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the picker card, or relabel it to what it does ("Open a client's agents" / "Jump to a client") and remove the Play icon so it stops reading as a run affordance. The run route that works is the per-agent Run button below it.

findings.title: Bind control offers agents the server is guaranteed to refuse
findings.clickPath: As staff on client A, AI Agents → "Agent setup" → the "Set up an agent for this client…" dropdown lists per-client agent instances baked under client B's lab folder → pick one → Add → the server refuses with "… runs only for the client whose lab repo slug is \"b\" …". This is the F131 shape the rest of the cluster is careful about: every other gate on these surfaces is evaluated server-side and painted before the press.

findings.title: Blocked-run reason says "Making a post now" on a clip maker and a Reddit agent
findings.clickPath: Open a live-bound clip-maker or Reddit agent whose umbrella has no templates yet → the primary control correctly reads "Create a new clip" / "Create a new reply", and the warning box immediately under it reads "Your Karos team is still setting up the formats this agent writes. Making a post now works once they are in place."
findings.detail: `AgentDetailPanel` resolves the output noun by archetype (`OUTPUT_NOUN`, agent-detail-panel.tsx:25-29, applied at :175, :179, :190, :301) precisely because "'Create a new post' is wrong on a clip maker and wrong on a Reddit agent". The fallback block reason beside it is archetype-blind: `noRunnableTemplateReason` returns post-only wording (src/lib/client-agent-runs.ts:188-190) and is used at agent-detail-panel.tsx:120-122. The empty-registry path is not an edge case for these two shapes — a clip-maker umbrella binds with no templates by design (agent-detail-panel.tsx:220-223) and `bindAsLive` writes `templates: []` for every non-X agent (src/lib/actions/client-agent-actions.ts:193-201). On a Reddit agent the sentence also reads as a claim that the portal will post.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass the noun (or the archetype) into `noRunnableTemplateReason` and use it in both branches of the returned string, so the reason and the button it explains always name the same output.

findings.title: Inputs-band rows hover like links but are not clickable
findings.clickPath: Open an intake-driven agent → "What it runs on" → hover a row (e.g. a named seat marked "Empty") → its border lights up neon → clicking does nothing; the only way in is the single link under the whole list.
